entries.pattern: (\d+)% increased spell damage with spells that cost life
examples: 40% increased Spell Damage with Spells that cost Life
entries.source_note: Game text of the Blood Mage passives (e.g. 40% / 12% / 6% increased Spell Damage with Spells that cost Life). A spell costs Life when its Life cost, after conversions, is at least 1: the engine's LifeCost stat, set before damage by calc::perform. PoB2 reads the same condition as a StatThreshold over LifeCost; used only as a cross-check.

entries.pattern: attacks using your weapons have added physical damage equal to (\d+)% of the accuracy rating on the weapon
examples: Attacks using your Weapons have Added Physical Damage equal to 25% of the Accuracy Rating on the Weapon
entries.source_note: Game text of the Amazon passive Penetrate. Each weapon adds to its own attacks: the Accuracy Rating on a weapon is the total of that item's own '+N to Accuracy Rating' lines (AccuracyOn<slot>, set by pobr-build inject_build_multipliers), and the added damage applies in that hand's pass (MainHandAttack / OffHandAttack). The same amount is added to minimum and maximum. PoB2 models it the same way; used only as a cross-check.

entries.pattern: minions have (\d+)% chance to inflict withered on hit
examples: Minions have 10% chance to inflict Withered on Hit
entries.source_note: Game text of the passive Wither Away's neighbours. The chance is the minions': a character without minions cannot inflict Withered with it, so the flag goes to the minions (read by calc::withered::apply_withered from each minion). PoB2 gives the flag to the player, which applies the configured Withered stacks to a character with no minions; PoBR differs on purpose.

entries.pattern: spells have a (\d+)% chance to inflict withered for (\d+) seconds on hit
examples: Spells have a 25% chance to inflict Withered for 4 seconds on Hit
entries.source_note: Game text of The Wicked Quill. Only the character's spells inflict the Withered, so the flag carries the Spell flag and is read under the calculated skill's flags by calc::withered::apply_withered. The chance and the duration say how fast stacks build, which the stated stack count (config) stands for.

entries.pattern: removes (\d+(?:\.\d+)?)% of life recovered from mana when used
entries.source_note: Local flask property: each use takes this percentage of the flask's total Life recovery away from Mana. Read per flask slot as Flask<N>ManaRemovedOnUse = percentage x Flask<N>Recovery; the amount is per use, with no use frequency or net Mana model assumed (no in-game test). The recovery itself is kept. The generic path read the line as FlaskRecovery BASE -15 on the flask, which is not the stat's meaning.
examples: Removes 15% of Life Recovered from Mana when used

entries.pattern: (\d+(?:\.\d+)?)% of chaos damage you prevent when hit recouped as life and mana(?: during effect)?
entries.source_note: Assumption, no in-game test: the Chaos damage a hit 'prevents' is the Chaos damage entering the Chaos mitigation stage (after taken-as shifts) minus what leaves it, so Chaos resistance and Chaos damage reduction count, negative resistance prevents nothing, and flat damage taken and later damage-taken multipliers do not. Blocked/deflected hits contribute nothing. The same percentage is recouped as Life and as Mana, each over its own recoup duration at its own recovery rate. 'During effect' is the charm's enabled-item convention (active charm within the charm limit), not an uptime model. See maintainer guide and defence::prevented_recoup.
examples: 50% of Chaos damage you prevent when Hit Recouped as Life and Mana during effect
